title: PLANT says unauthorized access to its e-money contractor's server leaked PLANT Pay records
date_note: The articles say the contractor found the anomalies and reported to PLANT on 20 November; the access ran from late 19 November to early 20 November.
geo_basis: Headquarters in Sakai, Fukui Prefecture, as stated by Fukui Shimbun
summary: PLANT, a Fukui-based company, said a third party accessed without authorization the server of a contractor that operates its PLANT Pay e-money service. According to PLANT, records were leaked, including card numbers and PIN numbers. PLANT says account passwords were not leaked and, as of 24 November, no fraudulent use had been confirmed.
plain: A contractor's server for the PLANT Pay e-money service was accessed without authorization. PLANT says records leaked, including card and PIN numbers, and has not confirmed any misuse as of 24 November.
exec: A supplier's server breach exposed e-money records, including card and PIN numbers, according to PLANT.
action: PLANT advises customers to be wary of suspicious emails, SMS or calls impersonating PLANT, and says card number and PIN can be reissued on request.

evidence.quote: 漏えいが確認された件数は4万2,107件である。

validation.note: Fukui Shimbun Online and Cybersecurity.com (Japan) are independent publishers that both state the contractor-server access and the leak, quoting PLANT. PLANT own notice (TDnet) could not be read.

review.note: Facts match Fukui Shimbun and Cybersecurity.com (Japan), but build errors figure-no-evidence for 42,107: the pages write 4万2,107件 / 4万2107件, so no word-for-word quote with the digit form exists; PLANT's own notice unreadable (TDnet 403)
